TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 23
At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain valid insofar as they do not conflict with this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 20
(1) Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to administer protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

CHAPTER IV
SCOPE
Article 4
The scope of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence includes:
a. implementation of protection for women and children, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. regulation of institutions and mechanisms for implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence.

CHAPTER III
OBJECTIVES
Article 3
The objective of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to guarantee the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of women and children as well as families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, and prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

6.8.rationale: Pasal 5 ayat (1) includes "anak berhadapan dengan hukum" (children in conflict with the law) as a covered situation. This does not establish an intersectional focus on women’s legal-process involvement; it is about children, and it is a broad scope statement rather than a tailored approach for legal-process-involved women. The English candidates reflect the Indonesian accurately. The judge incorrectly treated the mention of children in conflict with the law as satisfying the indicator, producing a false positive.
